page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized, burstable cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, it features 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The architecture integrates a substantial 480 MB L3 cache alongside 32 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, establishing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Hardware feature flags include support for AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 matrix instructions, AES cryptography, and total memory encryption. Local NVMe storage is not included, while baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier efficiency in single-threaded text processing and small-model inference tasks. The instance demonstrates strong single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2160.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.22 GB/sec. Text processing workloads perform in the top 10% tier, achieving 2933.0 on Geekbench text processing and 378.91 tokens/sec during text generation on 135M parameter language models. Multi-core execution and uncached memory bandwidth scores reside within the middle 50% average across standard synthetic benchmarks. The burstable CPU allocation provides flexibility for variable compute demands, though prolonged continuous compute bursts may experience throttling depending on credit availability.

The burstable flex architecture provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-intensive workloads experiencing variable duty cycles. By delivering high-frequency processing and specialized instruction sets like AMX without requiring dedicated full-time execution capacity, resource density is optimized. This instance configuration is well aligned with text analysis pipelines, light LLM text generation, software build engines, and elastic web application backends.
